detail.text: Everything in the Erdős argument is proved in the partial filed on this node: the Lambert identity Σ_{n∈B} 1/(2^n−1) = Σ_m f_B(m)/2^m (mimicking Mathlib's tsum_pow_div_one_sub_eq_tsum_sigma with an indicator weight), the doubling lemma f_B(p·r) = 2 f_B(r) for a prime p ≡ 1 (mod P) with p ∤ r (the divisors of p·r are the d and the p·d, and p·d ≡ d mod P), its iteration 2^|S| | f_B(n), the integer tail b·Σ f_B(j+i)/2^i, the CRT construction, the coprimality of the window with the modulus, and the…

route.text: Erdős 1948 (the A = ℕ proof on variant-2f5236aa) with f_B(m) = #{d | m : d ∈ B} in place of d(m): Lambert identity for a set, CRT placement of primes ≡ 1 (mod the period) so 2^m | f_B on windows, divisor-average contradiction
